stories.title: New paper "SplatAnything" fixes Gaussian spacing errors in 3D scene reconstruction
stories.summary: A new paper finds that feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting models suffer from inconsistent Gaussian spacing across scenes, and proposes SplatAnything to normalize it and fix ambiguous training supervision.
stories.more: Existing feed-forward 3DGS methods predict Gaussian attributes in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry. The paper argues this leaves the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers free to vary substantially across different scene scales and camera configurations. That mismatch causes systematic shifts in the targets used to train Gaussian scale, producing ambiguous supervision during training. SplatAnything is proposed as a fix for this, though the excerpt does not detail its exact mechanism or report benchmark results.

stories.title: Paper proposes P²-MOPD to speed up multi-teacher model distillation
stories.summary: A new paper introduces P²-MOPD, which jointly optimizes mixing coefficients and student weights to accelerate multi-teacher on-policy distillation of AI models.
stories.more: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation combines multiple expert models' capabilities by having a student model learn from trajectories it generates itself under supervision. The paper contrasts this with task arithmetic, which combines expert knowledge through training-free linear parameter combinations instead. P²-MOPD treats the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model, jointly optimizing the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective. The authors say this goes beyond what simple linear task arithmetic can do, though the excerpt does not give benchmark comparisons.

stories.title: New benchmark LongBanana tests long-context, multi-reference AI image generation
stories.summary: Researchers release LongBanana, described as the first expert-verified benchmark for long-context, multi-reference image synthesis, testing whether models can combine many reference images into one coherent result.
stories.more: LongBanana targets the emerging area of agent-driven image generation, where models must synthesize one image from multiple scattered reference sources. The benchmark contains 90 tasks organized in a 3-by-3 taxonomy, with each task including roughly 32 reference images. Tasks require retrieving dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractor images, binding entities and relations correctly, and composing a single coherent final image. The authors describe it as expert-designed and expert-verified, though the excerpt does not specify which models were evaluated or how they performed.

stories.title: Paper presents structure-aware kernels for faster relative-position attention
stories.summary: A new paper proposes structure-aware kernels to make relative-position attention, an alternative to RoPE used in transformers, faster and exact, especially in domains like audio.
stories.more: Relative-position attention mechanisms modify attention scores by adding content-position or bias-position terms, offering an alternative to RoPE across transformer architectures. The paper notes these mechanisms perform especially well in domains such as audio. Unlike RoPE, which encodes position through per-token rotations applied directly to queries and keys, relative-position terms typically require pairwise offset-dependent computation or lookups. The authors say this complicates integrating them efficiently, and propose structure-aware kernels to address it, though the excerpt cuts off before describing the kernels' design or reporting speedups.

stories.title: Nvidia espionage scandal undercuts Huang's lobbying against stricter chip export curbs
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted an affair with a woman US intelligence suspects is a Chinese informant, weakening his lobbying against tighter AI chip export controls as a new Congress prepares more scrutiny.
stories.more: Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation following Huang's admission of the affair. The affair is seen as weakening Huang's lobbying efforts against stricter US export controls on AI chips to China. A newly elected Democratic Congress is expected to increase scrutiny of AI chip smuggling to China and push for tighter restrictions. The article does not say when the affair began or what the board's investigation will examine.

stories.title: Authors turn to 'paper trail' tools to fight AI authorship allegations
stories.summary: As publishers grow suspicious about whether manuscripts were AI-generated, some authors are adopting 'paper trail' tools meant to document their writing process and defend against accusations.
stories.more: The publishing industry has grown increasingly paranoid about the provenance of manuscripts, questioning whether they were written by humans or AI. In response, some authors are using 'paper trail' tools intended to prove their own writing process. The article frames writers as caught in an impossible bind, and questions whether these defensive tools are actually enough to settle the allegations they face.

items.title: Authors Can Defend Against AI Allegations With ‘Paper Trail’ Tools. Is It Enough?
items.excerpt: As the publishing industry wrestles with paranoia over the provenance of manuscripts, writers are caught in an impossible bind.

stories.title: Bikers and bug conservationists join forces to oppose new Google data center
stories.summary: An unusual coalition of motorcyclists and insect conservationists is organizing against Google's plan to build a large new data center east of London, amid a wave of data center protests across Europe.
stories.more: Protests against data center construction have been breaking out across Europe. Near London, an unusual coalition of campaigners, including biker groups and bug conservation activists, has formed to try to block Google from building a sprawling new facility east of the city. The excerpt does not detail the specific environmental or community concerns driving the opposition beyond the scale of the proposed site.

items.title: Bikers and Bug-Lovers Join Forces to Fight a New Google Data Center
items.excerpt: As data center protests break out across Europe, a mismatched band of campaigners is trying to block Google from building a sprawling new facility east of London.
